title: UK 13 A plug fuse replacement
diagnosis: A blown fuse is the most common reason a plug stops working, and it's a safe home fix when the plug is unplugged. We'll open the fuse door, swap in a fuse of the right rating, and test it.
tools_needed: replacement BS 1362 cartridge fuse (3 A or 13 A, matching the appliance)
safety_notes: Keep the plug out of the socket for the whole repair until the final step.
Only use a proper BS 1362 cartridge fuse of the correct rating, never foil, wire or a nail.
If the plug is scorched, melted, cracked or the fuse blows again straight away, stop and replace the plug or cable, or call an electrician.

steps.title: Unplug the plug
steps.instruction: Switch off at the wall socket and pull the plug fully out. Keep it out of the socket until the final step.
steps.expected_visual_state: The plug is held in your hand, away from any socket, with the cable hanging free.
common_mistakes: Pulling on the cable instead of gripping the plug body
Leaving the plug in the socket while working

steps.title: Prise open the fuse door
steps.instruction: Put a small flat screwdriver in the notch at the cable end of the fuse door and lever it up. There is no screw to undo.
steps.expected_visual_state: The fuse door on the back of the plug is lifted open, showing the fuse underneath.
common_mistakes: Looking for a screw that does not exist
Levering at the wrong end and slipping the screwdriver
Trying to open the moulded body itself

steps.title: Remove the old fuse
steps.instruction: Lift the old fuse out of its two brass clips with the screwdriver tip or your fingers. Look at the wire inside for a break or blackening.
steps.expected_visual_state: The old fuse is held out of the plug and the empty brass clips are visible.
common_mistakes: Bending the brass clips while levering the fuse
Dropping the fuse into the plug cavity

steps.title: Choose the right replacement
steps.instruction: Check your appliance's power rating. Use a 3 A fuse for lamps, chargers and TVs up to about 700 W, or a 13 A fuse for heaters and kettles.
steps.expected_visual_state: A new BS 1362 cartridge fuse of the correct rating is held next to the plug.
common_mistakes: Fitting a 13 A fuse in a low-power appliance plug
Using foil, wire or a nail instead of a fuse

steps.title: Fit the new fuse
steps.instruction: Press the new fuse firmly into both brass clips until it sits snugly.
steps.expected_visual_state: The new fuse sits level across both brass clips with no gap at either end.
common_mistakes: Seating it in only one clip

steps.title: Close the fuse door
steps.instruction: Line up the fuse door and press it down until it clicks shut.
steps.expected_visual_state: The fuse door lies flush with the plug back and the fuse is hidden.
common_mistakes: Closing it before the fuse is fully seated
Stopping before you hear the click

steps.title: Plug in and test
steps.instruction: Only now push the plug into the wall socket, switch on, and turn on the appliance. Check it works.
steps.expected_visual_state: The plug is in the socket and the appliance powers on normally.
common_mistakes: Testing before the fuse door is closed
Ignoring a fuse that blows again straight away, which means a deeper fault
